transcript: Interview Guide. Activity E. FGD:  Aspirations of Youth
Module 1:  Agency, education and innovation (1 hour)

Position of the majority of young [sex of FGD] on the ladder of power and freedom (private rating): 5 = Power and freedom to make almost all major life decisions: 2 votes; 4 = Power and freedom to make many major life decisions: 0 votes; 3 = Power and freedom to make some major life decisions: 6 votes; 2 = Only a small amount of power and freedom: 1 vote; 1 = Almost no power or freedom to make decisions: 1 vote
(Result of secret voting)

Most of the people in our village are from middle class families. People here cannot avail higher education. After reaching intermediate level at best, they are often required to leave study for the sake of the family. Maximum people of this society cannot enjoy the facilities of life completely.

In fact in our village a very small portion of people are from lower and upper class. Here, those from 3rd step struggle hard to progress in life. From the viewpoint of educational background, middle class people reach up to intermediate (12th grade) or degree level (14th grade). Those from lower class do not try. While others work in order to improve their lifestyle, they can hardly meet their basic needs.

Due to various reasons, people fail to bear the expenses. And when that happens, they opt for job or business. An individual can inform his parents about his marriage only if he has a job. Otherwise he cannot do that.
Besides this, if he is involved in agricultural activities or business, he can take decision regarding his marriage.

In reality almost everyone in our society belongs to the middle class. More than 50% of the population falls under the 3rd level. People from this level study, run business and are engaged in agriculture and the father of the household takes most of the decisions.

Here the freedom of work exists. Freedom of doing agricultural activities is also evident. Other than these, father is the decision maker. 70% inhabitants of this village cast their vote according to the will of their parents.
I think those who voted for number 5 thought of themselves as independent individuals. But in effect they are not.
Education is essential. (10 people unanimously agreed to this) It is required to gain knowledge and to keep pace with society.
An educated person is well adopted in the society.
Education is important to run business too.
Long gone are the days of ignorance. Now days, education is required in every single aspect of our life. Hence I think my son must receive complete education.
Many girls do not consider marrying illiterate persons these days. Hence education is also required in case of marriage.

I believe if an illiterate boy marries an educated girl, their conjugal life might be happy. In that case the boy can learn from his wife. On the other hand, if an illiterate boy marries another illiterate girl; their mutual understanding won’t be that good.

No, I do not agree to this. (5 out of 10 people do not agree with the previous statement by one respondent) because they think it is not possible to run the family by dint of the girl’s knowledge. And also a boy would not agree to receive education from his wife.
Currently boys here study at least up to SSC (Secondary School Certificate).
Boys here are required to study up to SSC.
In order to keep up with the society, the boys should pass SSC.
Currently girls here study at least up to SSC.
Girls are usually married off at young age. Their family considers them as burden. That’s because girls cannot help out their families like the boys do.
In our village girls are married off when they are matured.
Some of the respondents said No, they aren’t. They are rather married off at a younger age because parents think of it as their responsibility. One said “The sooner, the better.”
Boys should study up to University or Degree level and girls up to Intermediate or Honors.
Boys should study as much as possible because education has no alternative. For girls, when they are married they depend on their husband.
80% people currently show commitment to educate both male and female children equally.

If there are two children both of them are sent to school. But after a certain time when they grow up, only the male child continue studying. The daughter is married off thinking she has reached the appropriate age for marriage.

I think this concept changes with time. For instance, earlier people used to think that studying is not required at all. At present they consider educating their daughters initially. But when the daughters reach their adolescence they change their minds. They marry them off despite their initial decision of educating their daughters.
Very few women passed SSC before. Suppose there are only 30 of them.

Preference for educating sons was 100% whereas for daughters it was only 30%. At present education for women is free of cost. Hence many girls are utilizing the opportunity. In the current year number of boys passing the SSC is equal to that of the girls.
A boy first learns to cut grass for cow feed at the age of 6 to 8.
At the age of 12 to 13 he starts cleaning weeds with his father. Soon he learns to take the responsibility of agricultural activities.
Though most learn at the age of 12-13, I learned when I was 15.
I gave fertilizer into the land when I was 13 because I knew I could do that.
Most of the boys here are able to sow the seeds at the age of only 17 or 18.It is one of the most important activities of cultivation.
Girls learn to thresh rice crop. They can do this along with their mothers.
Girls prepare firms for cattle or hen. They dump cow dung and collect straw or grass for the cows.
At the age of 13-14, girls can plant pea/ bottle gourd plants.
Due to financial insolvency girls often give up studying.
In a family with 5 to 6 brothers/sisters they are required to work hard in order to meet the basic needs. Hence they are deprived of education.
A person’s mental condition is related to his financial status.
Due to drug addiction or bad company boys often give up studying.

Many boys waste their time in affairs. Some of them engage themselves in eve teasing. In that case girls lodge complaints against them to the parents. And parents do not allow the boys to study any further.
Some of the boys from wealthy background get addicted to cigarettes, Opium, Yaba, Phensedyl, and Heroin etc. These have a devastating impact on their education.
The first reason behind this financial insolvency and everyone agreed unanimously to this statement.

The second reason is the influence of bad company. They offer their phone numbers to girls with the intention being engaged in an affair. And upon receiving complains from girls their parents put a stop on their schooling.
One said when there are many family members to feed education is hardly provided.
One also said that people go for earning money instead of studying.
In many cases minimum requirement for doing a job is completion of SSC. So, after passing SSC many people search for jobs instead of studying any further.
Many people go to XX in search of jobs. Many of them work as day laborers.
Some of them go for agricultural activities while some of them earn by means of cheating.
70% people cannot continue studies due to financial crisis. They promise to educate their children, so that they never have to suffer the way they did.
40% out of them go to XX. They earn their livelihood by means of business or physical labor.
I did not continue my study only because of poverty. I myself wished to earn money too. That’s why I shifted to XX. Now I am an earning member of my family.

Those who leave or need to leave studies have two options. They can do job at garments factory and also continue their study at Bangladesh Open University. This serves both the purposes of education and earning. At Open University, students need to attend the class only once a week.

I think it’s very important to listen to parents. It’s better to stay here than going to XX as many of them got spoiled after going to XX. If someone earns 10000 there, he sends only 2000 taka home. Rest of the money is spent somewhere else. So it’s even better to be a day laborer in the village than going there.
Corn and wheat seeds are available.
Seeds of “40-korola” are available.
Paddy harvesting machine is available.
Several varieties of seeds including Shakti, Super, Tej, Dhani Gold, 62 etc. are available.
Cotton cultivation is being done
Machine for threshing the rice crops are available.
Various pesticides are also available
Due to all these, agricultural growth has been amplified. Previously, wheat was not so available but now the production has increased.
New varieties of fertilizers are available for example boron, improved zinc fertilizer, TSP, DAP etc.

Beside all these, CIMMYT provided necessary training for corn and wheat cultivation. I myself participated once. The training was very beneficial. The training taught us like how much distance should be maintained among the plants and rows of plants. How to apply fertilizer in relation to the amount of land etc. Training is provided from trial plot to field level.
Among these the most important thing for the males is wheat seed. Then comes the developed training.

If the seed is better then the production will be better. This increased production will increase solvency and thus peacefulness in the family. Ultimately it will result in advancing from 3rd level of the ladder to the 5th one.
The training is required to know whether the seeds have been sown in the suitable time.
It has been helpful for girls in case of threshing the crops.
If women are knowledgeable, they can discuss with the men if any mistake occur. Women cannot go there but they can definitely provide suggestions.
Women can participate in training programs. When the training was offered 4-5 girls took part on a limited seats.
The training took place at XX on poultry.
Guardians do not encourage participation of females in such activities. This is because of their religious sentiment.
Module 2.  Gender norms, livelihoods, and family formation (1 ½ hours)
Previously wheat fields were not being irrigated but now it is in practice.
Earlier there were no hybrids and seeds had to be sown manually.
There was no training on cultivation. People used to cultivate in whatever way they deemed right.
No fertilizer, pesticides/disinfectants were available.
In our village we did not have quality wheat seeds. But now we do.
Currently we have wheat seeds of better quality, training sessions, machines etc.
Modern machines for sowing and threshing wheat are available now. Qualities of pesticides, fertilizers etc. have also improved.
Things have definitely improved over time. This change has been possible because of CIMMYT.
Training conducted by different associations helped improve the standard. Production has almost doubled.
Previously hardly 1 mon (40 KG) of crops could be produced in a 1 katha (1 katha=20 bigha) land. Now the production has increased to3 mons.
Modern technology has increased farming efficiency and has made it possible for farmers to work their farms with fewer people and labor.
People have become more conscious than before.
In our village the roles of male and females are always fixed. Discrimination is prevalent here. But this is mainly because of our religious values and norms.
The convention here is not to let women do the fieldwork.
Here women do not participate in agricultural activities at all. If a family allows, then female members can work outside; the society looks down upon that family. Others blame the family members.
No female work in the field
Discrimination prevails. Girls do not take part in farming.
If there is no male member in the family they must lease their land to someone.
If the girl is educated then the scenario is different. She is treated with respect. If she works for an NGO it’s not a problem. Yet she is not allowed to work in the field.
If a female grows crop and tries to sell on her own she will face obstacles from her family. But if she tries really hard she can do that against other’s will.
If they know how to grow vegetables in homestead gardening, they can sell them somewhere near their house.
Besides all these if she still requires a helping hand, she can have a vendor come to her own home for sale. But she is still not allowed to go to the hut (Local Market place) and sell the crops.
This is in fact our social and religious custom, which we have been observing from times immemorial.
Parents will definitely object to this and everyone strongly agrees to this.
Religious norms in this regard are very strong here.
If it is for boys then there would be no such problem. Rather his parents will encourage him.
Women generally do not own the plots. They to not take the decisions but provide suggestions at times
Each plot is different from the other and is suitable for different crops. Hence someone having adequate knowledge regarding this decides what to do.
The elders decide how to manage the plots.
The family members collectively take the decision. Elderly and experienced women also take part in the discussion.
Father takes the main decision. He also consults with others if necessary. (6 respondents stated that only father takes the decision and 4 stated that both father and mother take the decision.)
We do not have any such obligation. No separate arrangement for this is done in our village.
Cultivation is same irrespective of the owner of the plot.
Whether the owner is mother or father, it’s father who takes the decisions regarding the cultivation.
This usually happens in female-centered families. She might consult with her paternal/maternal uncle or eldest son. She might also seek advice from neighbors.
Male farmers usually consult with the experienced and skilled farmers of the region. Some might also consult with their wives.
Many discuss with their husbands’ uncle or brother-in-law.
Male farmers some time decide by themselves. They also ask their wives or eldest sons.
I think Adam would not respond to that.
I think Adam would not allow Ana and ask her to stay in the house.
Women should be doing household chores.
I don’t think he would approve this.

I think he would respond to Ana’s request. Because the group is agriculture based. I would certainly allow my wife to join the group. But if the group were not agriculture based, I wouldn’t have allowed.
If the group were formed for cultivation purpose then I would allow.
If it were NGO, club or any other association I would not allow her. But if it were agriculture based, I would permit. (10 out of 10 agreed to this statement)
Impossible. He would not allow at all.
He would not allow no matter how much profit this could earn. He would say, “You don’t need to cultivate anything at all. “(10 out of 10 strongly affirmed this)
He will not ask for help.
If the income is sufficient then he will not ask for help from her. He will do the work all by himself to the best of his ability.(All of them agreed to this satement)
She will have little reputation in our society.
She will have no dignity at all in this society.
She will have no reputation in the village.
She won’t have any social status.
Mark’s friends and other people in the village will hardly respect him.
His friends might maintain communication with him; but they will definitely think lowly of Mark.
His friends won’t respect him at all.
Mark will not accept that positively even if it’s profitable for him.
In our village, Mark would not allow her to do that in the first place.(Everyone agreed to this)
Listen, my sister does not do any work but I do.
There is no gender equity. For instance I’m allowed to go to the market but my sister isn’t allowed to do so. How can you call that equity?

As a matter of fact it is not possible to promote gender equity everywhere. Because women should not go the market. They should take care of the children and manage the household chores. And the males are required to work outside for his family.
What is equity? I will get my father’s land but my sister won’t get anything. Again boys are required to do all the works whereas girls do nothing. Is that equity?
Equity means both of them will hard equally and enjoy the facilities together.
Boys inherit more properties than girls. This is an age-old custom.
This is not an age-old custom. This has been dictated by Islam. Our religion has ensured equity in some cases but not in all cases.
According to Islam, if a girl inherits 1 acre of land, a boy will inherit 2 acres (double). This is done based on religious regulations, not government laws.
Gender equity is good but not from the Islamic point of view.
We should not bring gender equity everywhere. We may apply this in few cases.
We can apply the concept of equity when marrying off our daughter. But due to religious limitations girls aren’t allowed to go outside in fields, vegetable gardens, markets etc.
The husband would take this decision.
No, the wife would decide. (7 of the respondents think husband would decide, 3 of them think wife would.)
One respondent asked another, “Let’s think practically, shall we? Is your mother allowed to sell anything without the consent of your father?”
She might ask to keep 1 kg for the requirement of family and take the other 7 kg.
In this situation, David is more likely to sell the vegetables. (Everyone agreed)
That’s because he knows the market rate well. So, this would be more profitable for the family.
If the woman were to receive the money she would ask her husband not to sell everything.
She will be given the chance once. However, if they incur loss, her husband will bully her.(Everyone agreed)
If they earn profit they will follow this method. Her husband may present a saree to his sister-in-law as well.

How easy or difficult for Diana to purchase the plot of land without David’s support (private rating): 1 = Very easy: 1 vote; 2 = Easy: 1 vote; 3 = Neither easy nor difficult: 2 votes; 4 = Difficult: 3 votes; 5 = Very difficult: 3 votes
Because that goes against the will of the husband
Since this money is not the result of his own hard work; the husband would want to spend it for his amusement.
There is a possibility of conjugal fight. So it’s very difficult.
If they care for each other this should be easy.

How easy or difficult for David to purchase the motorbike without Diana’s support (private rating): 1 = Very easy: 3 votes; 2 = Easy: 2 votes; 3 = Neither easy nor difficult: 5 votes; 4 = Difficult: 0 votes; 5 = Very difficult: 0 votes
Since the husband owns the money he can do whatever he wishes to.
If the wife protests her husband will abuse her
It will be really difficult for the wife to say anything against her husband.
No, a young woman cannot walk alone in a market.
A young woman will never go to the market alone even by mistake. If she has to go she will have someone to accompany her.
Boys might eve tease her.
They cannot do so due to social restrictions.
Besides, religion also plays a role here.
If a young woman walks alone in a local market everybody will criticize her. It will be hard to marry her off.
People will say, “This girl roams around in market, I can’t marry her.”
When a woman is unmarried and live with her parents, the parents are often lenient. She can go to the market accompanied by a kid. But this is totally impossible once she gets married.
Women are not allowed to use phone after marriage. Even if she is allowed to keep a mobile it is not recharged by anyone.
If her husband lives abroad it’s impossible too.
This is impossible due to our religious norms. People harshly criticize if any woman does so.
She will never be allowed to sell in the local market. This is totally incredible.
Here they have no social or religious freedom.
It is tough for the men. There’s no guarantee that he will get a job there.
He must seek help from a relative/ known person in order to get a job.
He definitely needs a channel or medium.
It’s better if he has close relatives or friends over there.
He should keep in his mind that the place he is heading to should have accommodation, food, transport and other facilities. Also the city must have job opportunities.
His friends will demean him.
His family members might be happy but friends or society will disparage him.
People are satisfied if the boy works hard. But if he sits idle after returning home they will criticize him.
Many are reluctant to offer him any job.
The boy still has the opportunity to cultivate lands.
If he is a farmer’s son he already knows firming. So it gets easier for him to cultivate.
But if he is not so active or good for nothing he barely has any job opportunity.
Males usually marry at the age of 22 or 23.
10% of the females get married at the age of 13. 50% of them at the age of 14 or 15. 30% females marry when they are 16 to 18 years old.
Rest of the 10% females gets married within 25. That means after completion or in the middle of higher education.
And males marry at the age of 16 to 23. In this case, boys from financially solvent background marry after completing their education or getting a job.
Parents take the decision regarding marriages in case of 90% families.
Rest 10% marries according to their own choice.
I think one should get married based on the decision of his family.(10 out of 10 agreed)
In our community, women typically have their first child at the age of 17-18.
80% women have their first child at the age of 16-17.
Rest 20% women have their first child at the age of 15-16.
A very few number of women get married later. They usually have their first child at the age of 20 or even later than that.
It’s ok to have the first child at the age of 17 or 18. But having child at a younger age might be harmful for both the baby and the mother.
I think 20 is the most appropriate age for a women to have her first child. That’s when a woman becomes capable of taking care of the child.
Husband and wife together take this decision.
This is definitely taken based on mutual consent.
There is nothing to decide when to have children. To marry means to have children. (Everyone laughed)
Previously family planning schemes were not so available. Even if they were available people were reluctant to implement them. But now-a-days people implement the scheme.
In future I definitely want to see a better and improved community
A society that will be educationally more advanced
I would like to see a village with 100% education rate. All the children must have the advantage of receiving higher education.
We do not want to be a backward nation. I want my daughter to pass B.Ed. or M.A.
We need more educational institutions in and around of our village.
Modern village, transportation system and roads, improved communication system, Internet facilities etc. are also our requirements. 3G Internet is not yet available in our area.
The most important thing that we are lacking is a college.
We not only want to educate our sons but also our daughters as well.
